_comment: Tier 2 validation rules (R2 7.2): checks the registry's structure cannot imply. Hand-authored. build.py merges these into logical_schemas.json, which is generated and must not be edited directly. Each rule's query returns offending rows; an empty result is a pass (R2 7.3).

analysis.spike_events.message: a spike precedes the start of the bucket it is labelled with
analysis.spike_events.sql: SELECT session_id, unit_id, t_tick, time_bucket_tick FROM analysis_spike_events WHERE time_bucket_tick > t_tick

analysis.spike_events.message: buckets overlap in tick range, so the layout they declare is not a partition
analysis.spike_events.sql: SELECT a.session_id, a.clock_id, a.time_bucket_tick AS earlier_bucket, a.hi, b.time_bucket_tick AS later_bucket, b.lo FROM (SELECT session_id, clock_id, time_bucket_tick, MIN(t_tick) AS lo, MAX(t_tick) AS hi FROM analysis_spike_events GROUP BY session_id, clock_id, time_bucket_tick) a JOIN (SELECT session_id, clock_id, time_bucket_tick, MIN(t_tick) AS lo, MAX(t_tick) AS hi FROM analysis_spike_events GROUP BY session_id, clock_id, time_bucket_tick) b ON a.session_id = b.session_id AND a.clock_id = b.clock_id AND b.time_bucket_tick > a.time_bucket_tick WHERE b.lo <= a.hi

core.array_assets.message: scaling is declared both on the array and per channel
core.array_assets.sql: SELECT a.array_asset_id FROM core_array_assets a WHERE a.conversion IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM core_array_channels c WHERE c.array_asset_id = a.array_asset_id AND c.conversion IS NOT NULL)

core.array_assets.message: sample_rate_hz disagrees with the time axis step
core.array_assets.sql: SELECT a.array_asset_id, a.sample_rate_hz FROM core_array_assets a JOIN core_array_dimensions d USING (array_asset_id) JOIN core_clocks c ON c.clock_id = d.clock_id WHERE a.sample_rate_hz IS NOT NULL AND d.step_tick_num / COALESCE(d.step_tick_den, 1) IS NOT NULL AND c.tick_rate_hz IS NOT NULL AND abs(a.sample_rate_hz - c.tick_rate_hz / d.step_tick_num / COALESCE(d.step_tick_den, 1)) > 1e-6

core.array_channels.message: a conversion without a unit yields a number in no known quantity
core.array_channels.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, channel_index FROM core_array_channels WHERE conversion IS NOT NULL AND unit IS NULL

core.array_dimensions.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, COUNT(*) AS n_axes, MAX(axis_index) AS max_axis FROM core_array_dimensions GROUP BY array_asset_id HAVING MAX(axis_index) <> COUNT(*) - 1 OR MIN(axis_index) <> 0

core.array_dimensions.message: an axis declares more than one coordinate form
core.array_dimensions.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, axis_index FROM core_array_dimensions WHERE (CASE WHEN origin_tick IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN origin_value IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN coordinate_array_asset_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN coordinate_resource IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 1

core.array_dimensions.message: a regular tick axis needs clock_id, origin_tick and step_tick_num
core.array_dimensions.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, axis_index FROM core_array_dimensions WHERE origin_tick IS NOT NULL AND (step_tick_num IS NULL OR clock_id IS NULL)

core.array_dimensions.message: a regular numeric axis needs origin_value, step_value and coordinate_unit
core.array_dimensions.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, axis_index FROM core_array_dimensions WHERE origin_value IS NOT NULL AND (step_value IS NULL OR coordinate_unit IS NULL)

core.array_dimensions.message: coordinate_resource and coordinate_position_column must be present together
core.array_dimensions.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, axis_index FROM core_array_dimensions WHERE (coordinate_resource IS NULL) <> (coordinate_position_column IS NULL)

core.array_dimensions.message: a core axis points outward at a non-core resource (R20 §5.1)
core.array_dimensions.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, axis_index, coordinate_resource FROM core_array_dimensions WHERE coordinate_resource IS NOT NULL AND coordinate_resource NOT LIKE 'core.%'

core.array_dimensions.message: a step denominator is not positive, so the step it defines is meaningless
core.array_dimensions.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, axis_index, step_tick_den FROM core_array_dimensions WHERE step_tick_den IS NOT NULL AND step_tick_den <= 0

core.array_dimensions.message: an axis declares one half of its labelled coordinates; the resource says where the positions are and the column says which of its columns holds them (R100 2.2)
core.array_dimensions.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, axis_index, coordinate_resource, coordinate_position_column FROM core_array_dimensions WHERE (coordinate_resource IS NULL) <> (coordinate_position_column IS NULL)

core.calibrations.message: a calibration declares one unit of measure and not the other; the pair is what makes a point readable (R89 §2.3)
core.calibrations.sql: SELECT calibration_id, input_unit, output_unit FROM core_calibrations WHERE (input_unit IS NULL) <> (output_unit IS NULL)

core.calibrations.message: a calibration carries points and declares no units, so nothing says what its values are measured in (R89 §2.3)
core.calibrations.sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.calibration_id FROM core_calibrations c JOIN core_calibration_points p USING (calibration_id) WHERE c.input_unit IS NULL OR c.output_unit IS NULL

core.clock_anchors.message: anchors are declared for a clock with no parent
core.clock_anchors.sql: SELECT DISTINCT a.clock_id FROM core_clock_anchors a JOIN core_clocks c USING (clock_id) WHERE c.parent_clock_id IS NULL
SELECT clock_id, COUNT(*) AS n, MAX(anchor_index) AS hi FROM core_clock_anchors GROUP BY clock_id HAVING MAX(anchor_index) <> COUNT(*) - 1 OR MIN(anchor_index) <> 0

core.clock_anchors.message: anchor sequences do not increase together, so interpolation is undefined
core.clock_anchors.sql: SELECT clock_id, anchor_index FROM ( SELECT *, LAG(t_tick) OVER (PARTITION BY clock_id ORDER BY anchor_index) AS prev_t, LAG(parent_tick) OVER (PARTITION BY clock_id ORDER BY anchor_index) AS prev_p FROM core_clock_anchors) WHERE prev_t IS NOT NULL AND (t_tick <= prev_t OR parent_tick <= prev_p)

core.clock_anchors.message: an anchor gap exceeds twice the median, leaving ticks the mapping does not define (R27 5.3)
core.clock_anchors.sql: WITH gaps AS (SELECT clock_id, anchor_index, t_tick - LAG(t_tick) OVER (PARTITION BY clock_id ORDER BY anchor_index) AS gap FROM core_clock_anchors), typical AS (SELECT clock_id, median(gap) AS m FROM gaps WHERE gap IS NOT NULL GROUP BY clock_id) SELECT g.clock_id, g.anchor_index, g.gap, t.m FROM gaps g JOIN typical t USING (clock_id) WHERE g.gap IS NOT NULL AND g.gap > t.m * 2

core.clock_observation_intervals.overlap_message: observation windows overlap, which would double-count observed time

core.clocks.message: neither tick_rate_hz nor an exact rational rate is present
core.clocks.sql: SELECT clock_id FROM core_clocks WHERE tick_rate_hz IS NULL AND (tick_rate_num IS NULL OR tick_rate_den IS NULL)

core.clocks.message: a clock declares both a float rate and a rational one (R95 §3.2)
core.clocks.sql: SELECT clock_id, tick_rate_hz, tick_rate_num, tick_rate_den FROM core_clocks WHERE tick_rate_hz IS NOT NULL AND tick_rate_num IS NOT NULL
SELECT clock_id, tick_rate_hz, tick_rate_num, tick_rate_den FROM core_clocks WHERE tick_rate_hz <= 0 OR tick_rate_num <= 0 OR tick_rate_den <= 0

core.clocks.message: transform_slope and transform_offset must be present together
core.clocks.sql: SELECT clock_id FROM core_clocks WHERE (transform_slope IS NULL) <> (transform_offset IS NULL)

core.clocks.message: a clock transform is declared without a parent clock
core.clocks.sql: SELECT clock_id FROM core_clocks WHERE parent_clock_id IS NULL AND transform_slope IS NOT NULL

core.clocks.message: tick_zero_utc is more than a day from session_start_time
core.clocks.sql: SELECT c.clock_id, c.tick_zero_utc, s.session_start_time FROM core_clocks c JOIN core_sessions s USING (session_id) WHERE c.tick_zero_utc IS NOT NULL AND s.session_start_time IS NOT NULL AND (c.tick_zero_utc < s.session_start_time - INTERVAL 1 DAY OR c.tick_zero_utc > s.session_start_time + INTERVAL 1 DAY)

core.clocks.message: a clock declares both a linear transform and anchor points
core.clocks.sql: SELECT c.clock_id FROM core_clocks c WHERE c.transform_slope IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM core_clock_anchors a WHERE a.clock_id = c.clock_id)

core.clocks.message: a clock is its own ancestor, so walking the chain does not terminate (R27 3)
core.clocks.sql: WITH RECURSIVE up(clock_id, ancestor, depth) AS (SELECT clock_id, parent_clock_id, 1 FROM core_clocks WHERE parent_clock_id IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT u.clock_id, c.parent_clock_id, u.depth + 1 FROM up u JOIN core_clocks c ON c.clock_id = u.ancestor WHERE c.parent_clock_id IS NOT NULL AND u.depth < 64) SELECT DISTINCT clock_id FROM up WHERE ancestor = clock_id OR depth >= 64

core.clocks.message: a non-reference clock declares no alignment, so it cannot be converted (R27 4)
core.clocks.sql: SELECT c.clock_id FROM core_clocks c JOIN core_sessions s USING (session_id) WHERE s.reference_clock_id IS NOT NULL AND c.clock_id <> s.reference_clock_id AND c.transform_slope IS NULL AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM core_clock_anchors a WHERE a.clock_id = c.clock_id)

core.clocks.message: a clock that is anchored or is the session's reference declares no observation interval, so nothing on it has a window to inherit (R98 3.1)
core.clocks.sql: SELECT c.session_id, c.clock_id FROM core_clocks c LEFT JOIN core_clock_observation_intervals o ON o.session_id = c.session_id AND o.clock_id = c.clock_id WHERE o.clock_id IS NULL AND (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM core_clock_anchors a WHERE a.session_id = c.session_id AND a.clock_id = c.clock_id) OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM core_sessions s WHERE s.session_id = c.session_id AND s.reference_clock_id = c.clock_id))

core.clocks.message: a clock with no anchors records the outcome of a terminal-anchor test that cannot have run on it (R99 3.2)
core.clocks.sql: SELECT c.session_id, c.clock_id FROM core_clocks c WHERE (c.withheld_first_anchor IS NOT NULL OR c.withheld_last_anchor IS NOT NULL) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM core_clock_anchors a WHERE a.session_id = c.session_id AND a.clock_id = c.clock_id)

core.devices.message: a device is its own ancestor, or its attachment chain does not terminate (R67 §2.3)
core.devices.sql: WITH RECURSIVE up(device_id, ancestor, depth) AS (SELECT device_id, parent_device_id, 1 FROM core_devices WHERE parent_device_id IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT u.device_id, d.parent_device_id, u.depth + 1 FROM up u JOIN core_devices d ON d.device_id = u.ancestor WHERE d.parent_device_id IS NOT NULL AND u.depth < 64) SELECT DISTINCT device_id FROM up WHERE ancestor = device_id OR depth >= 64

core.devices.message: one serial number appears on more than one device row; a device is the physical object (R67 §2.2)
core.devices.sql: SELECT serial_number, COUNT(*) AS n_rows FROM core_devices WHERE serial_number IS NOT NULL GROUP BY serial_number HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

core.event_stream_observation_intervals.overlap_message: observation windows overlap, which would double-count observed time

core.event_streams.message: streams carry no observation intervals and their clock declares none, so no rate over them has a denominator
core.event_streams.sql: SELECT s.event_stream_id, s.event_stream_name FROM core_event_streams s WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM core_event_stream_observation_intervals o WHERE o.event_stream_id = s.event_stream_id) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM core_clock_observation_intervals c WHERE c.session_id = s.session_id AND c.clock_id = s.clock_id)

core.events.message: events fall outside the observation window in force for their stream
core.events.sql: WITH stream_windows AS ( SELECT o.event_stream_id, o.start_tick, o.stop_tick FROM core_event_stream_observation_intervals o UNION ALL SELECT s.event_stream_id, c.start_tick, c.stop_tick FROM core_event_streams s JOIN core_clock_observation_intervals c ON c.session_id = s.session_id AND c.clock_id = s.clock_id WHERE NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM core_event_stream_observation_intervals o WHERE o.event_stream_id = s.event_stream_id ) ), observed AS ( SELECT DISTINCT event_stream_id FROM stream_windows ) SELECT e.session_id, e.stream_id, e.t_tick FROM core_events e JOIN observed k ON e.stream_id = k.event_stream_id LEFT JOIN stream_windows w ON e.stream_id = w.event_stream_id AND e.t_tick BETWEEN w.start_tick AND w.stop_tick WHERE w.start_tick IS NULL

core.media_assets.message: an asset declares one half of its presentation-timestamp rate; half a rational is unusable (R70 §2.2)
core.media_assets.sql: SELECT media_asset_id, pts_rate_num, pts_rate_den FROM core_media_assets WHERE (pts_rate_num IS NULL) <> (pts_rate_den IS NULL)

core.media_assets.message: frames carry pts for an asset that does not say what those timestamps count (R70 §2.2)
core.media_assets.sql: SELECT a.media_asset_id FROM core_media_assets a WHERE a.pts_rate_num IS NULL AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM core_media_frames f WHERE f.media_asset_id = a.media_asset_id AND f.pts IS NOT NULL)

core.media_assets.message: a presentation-timestamp rate is not positive
core.media_assets.sql: SELECT media_asset_id, pts_rate_num, pts_rate_den FROM core_media_assets WHERE pts_rate_num <= 0 OR pts_rate_den <= 0

core.media_frames.message: frame_index is not contiguous from 0 within an asset
core.media_frames.sql: SELECT media_asset_id, COUNT(*) AS n_frames, MAX(frame_index) AS max_index FROM core_media_frames GROUP BY media_asset_id HAVING MAX(frame_index) <> COUNT(*) - 1 OR MIN(frame_index) <> 0

core.media_frames.message: pts is not strictly increasing in frame_index order within an asset, so the frames are not numbered in presentation order (R69 §2.1)
core.media_frames.sql: SELECT media_asset_id, frame_index, pts, prev AS previous_pts FROM (SELECT media_asset_id, frame_index, pts, LAG(pts) OVER (PARTITION BY media_asset_id ORDER BY frame_index) AS prev FROM core_media_frames WHERE pts IS NOT NULL) WHERE prev IS NOT NULL AND pts <= prev

core.preferred_runs.message: a preference names a run whose activity_type differs from the preference's
core.preferred_runs.sql: SELECT p.session_id, p.activity_type, p.scope, r.activity_type FROM core_preferred_runs p JOIN core_processing_runs r USING (processing_run_id) WHERE r.activity_type IS DISTINCT FROM p.activity_type

core.preferred_runs.message: a preference names a run belonging to another session
core.preferred_runs.sql: SELECT p.session_id, p.processing_run_id, r.session_id FROM core_preferred_runs p JOIN core_processing_runs r USING (processing_run_id) WHERE r.session_id IS NOT NULL AND r.session_id IS DISTINCT FROM p.session_id

core.preferred_runs.message: the preferred run is superseded by another run
core.preferred_runs.sql: SELECT p.session_id, p.activity_type, p.scope, p.processing_run_id FROM core_preferred_runs p WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM core_processing_runs r WHERE r.supersedes_run_id = p.processing_run_id)

core.processing_runs.message: a failed run is recorded in a committed packet
core.processing_runs.sql: SELECT processing_run_id, activity_type FROM core_processing_runs WHERE status = 'failed'

core.processing_runs.message: a materialization run does not record the software that produced it
core.processing_runs.sql: SELECT processing_run_id, software_name, software_version FROM core_processing_runs WHERE activity_type = 'materialization' AND (software_name IS NULL OR software_version IS NULL)
SELECT processing_run_id FROM core_processing_runs WHERE supersedes_run_id = processing_run_id

core.processing_runs.message: the supersedes chain contains a cycle
core.processing_runs.sql: WITH RECURSIVE up(processing_run_id, ancestor, depth) AS (SELECT processing_run_id, supersedes_run_id, 1 FROM core_processing_runs WHERE supersedes_run_id IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT u.processing_run_id, r.supersedes_run_id, u.depth + 1 FROM up u JOIN core_processing_runs r ON r.processing_run_id = u.ancestor WHERE r.supersedes_run_id IS NOT NULL AND u.depth < 64) SELECT DISTINCT processing_run_id FROM up WHERE ancestor = processing_run_id OR depth >= 64

core.processing_runs.message: several runs share an activity and scope and none is preferred, so a consumer cannot choose between them (R82 §2.1)
core.processing_runs.sql: WITH grouped AS ( SELECT session_id, activity_type, scope, count(*) AS n FROM core_processing_runs WHERE scope IS NOT NULL GROUP BY session_id, activity_type, scope HAVING count(*) > 1) SELECT g.session_id, g.activity_type, g.scope, g.n FROM grouped g WHERE NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM core_preferred_runs p WHERE p.activity_type = g.activity_type AND p.scope = g.scope AND (p.session_id = g.session_id OR (p.session_id IS NULL AND g.session_id IS NULL)))

core.processing_runs.message: an activity has several runs and at least one records no scope, so whether they compete cannot be determined (R82 §2.2)
core.processing_runs.sql: WITH per_activity AS ( SELECT session_id, activity_type, count(*) AS n, count(*) FILTER (WHERE scope IS NULL) AS unscoped FROM core_processing_runs GROUP BY session_id, activity_type) SELECT session_id, activity_type, n, unscoped FROM per_activity WHERE n > 1 AND unscoped > 0

core.processing_runs.message: a run declares one half of its scope; the pair is what carries the meaning (R49 §2.4)
core.processing_runs.sql: SELECT processing_run_id, scope_kind, scope FROM core_processing_runs WHERE (scope IS NULL) <> (scope_kind IS NULL)

core.sessions.message: the manifest's session inventory and core.sessions disagree; the manifest names a session by its session_name, since an assigned session_id means nothing outside the packet that assigned it (R53 §2.3.1)
core.sessions.sql: SELECT session_name FROM core_sessions WHERE session_name NOT IN (SELECT session_id FROM manifest_sessions) UNION ALL SELECT session_id FROM manifest_sessions WHERE session_id NOT IN (SELECT session_name FROM core_sessions)
SELECT session_id, session_start_time, session_end_time FROM core_sessions WHERE session_end_time < session_start_time

core.sessions.message: a session declaring more than one clock names no reference clock (R27 2)
core.sessions.sql: SELECT s.session_id, COUNT(*) AS n_clocks FROM core_sessions s JOIN core_clocks c USING (session_id) WHERE s.reference_clock_id IS NULL GROUP BY s.session_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

core.sessions.message: a clock does not reach the session's reference clock, so it cannot be converted to it
core.sessions.sql: WITH RECURSIVE up(clock_id, ancestor, depth) AS (SELECT clock_id, clock_id, 0 FROM core_clocks UNION ALL SELECT u.clock_id, c.parent_clock_id, u.depth + 1 FROM up u JOIN core_clocks c ON c.clock_id = u.ancestor WHERE c.parent_clock_id IS NOT NULL AND u.depth < 64) SELECT c.session_id, c.clock_id FROM core_clocks c JOIN core_sessions s USING (session_id) WHERE s.reference_clock_id IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM up u WHERE u.clock_id = c.clock_id AND u.ancestor = s.reference_clock_id)

core.sessions.message: a session declares an alignment bound below R27 5.3's default of one median anchor interval, which reaches no further than declaring nothing (R99 3.1)
core.sessions.sql: SELECT session_id, alignment_bound FROM core_sessions WHERE alignment_bound < 1.0

core.sorting_run_channels.message: a contact appears more than once in one run's channel list
core.sorting_run_channels.sql: SELECT session_id, sorting_run_id, electrode_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM core_sorting_run_channels GROUP BY session_id, sorting_run_id, electrode_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

core.sorting_run_channels.message: channel_index is not contiguous from 0 within a run
core.sorting_run_channels.sql: SELECT session_id, sorting_run_id, COUNT(*) AS n, MAX(channel_index) AS hi FROM core_sorting_run_channels GROUP BY session_id, sorting_run_id HAVING MAX(channel_index) <> COUNT(*) - 1 OR MIN(channel_index) <> 0

core.spike_events.message: negative ticks on a clock with no absolute reference
core.spike_events.sql: SELECT u.session_id, u.clock_id, MIN(s.t_tick) AS min_tick FROM core_spike_events s JOIN core_units u USING (unit_id) JOIN core_clocks c ON c.clock_id = u.clock_id WHERE s.t_tick < 0 AND c.tick_zero_utc IS NULL GROUP BY u.session_id, u.clock_id

core.spike_events.message: spikes fall outside the observation window in force for their unit
core.spike_events.sql: WITH unit_windows AS ( SELECT o.unit_id, o.start_tick, o.stop_tick FROM core_unit_observation_intervals o UNION ALL SELECT u.unit_id, c.start_tick, c.stop_tick FROM core_units u JOIN core_clock_observation_intervals c ON c.session_id = u.session_id AND c.clock_id = u.clock_id WHERE NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM core_unit_observation_intervals o WHERE o.unit_id = u.unit_id ) ), observed AS ( SELECT DISTINCT unit_id FROM unit_windows ) SELECT s.session_id, s.unit_id, s.t_tick FROM core_spike_events s JOIN observed k ON s.unit_id = k.unit_id LEFT JOIN unit_windows w ON s.unit_id = w.unit_id AND s.t_tick BETWEEN w.start_tick AND w.stop_tick WHERE w.start_tick IS NULL

core.unit_electrodes.message: a unit designates more than one peak electrode (R28 2)
core.unit_electrodes.sql: SELECT unit_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM core_unit_electrodes WHERE is_primary GROUP BY unit_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

core.unit_electrodes.message: channel_index is not contiguous from 0, so a dense axis indexed by it addresses rows that are not there
core.unit_electrodes.sql: SELECT unit_id, COUNT(*) AS n, MAX(channel_index) AS hi FROM core_unit_electrodes WHERE channel_index IS NOT NULL GROUP BY unit_id HAVING MAX(channel_index) <> COUNT(*) - 1 OR MIN(channel_index) <> 0

core.unit_electrodes.message: a unit sits on an electrode its sorting run did not use
core.unit_electrodes.sql: SELECT ue.unit_id, ue.electrode_id FROM core_unit_electrodes ue JOIN core_units u ON ue.unit_id = u.unit_id JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT session_id, sorting_run_id FROM core_sorting_run_channels) d ON d.session_id = u.session_id AND d.sorting_run_id = u.sorting_run_id LEFT JOIN core_sorting_run_channels c ON c.session_id = u.session_id AND c.sorting_run_id = u.sorting_run_id AND c.electrode_id = ue.electrode_id WHERE c.electrode_id IS NULL

core.unit_observation_intervals.overlap_message: observation windows overlap, which would double-count observed time

core.unit_quality_labels.message: a (source, label) pair projects onto more than one normalized_label
core.unit_quality_labels.sql: SELECT source, label, COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(normalized_label, '')) AS distinct_projections FROM core_unit_quality_labels GROUP BY source, label HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(normalized_label, '')) > 1

core.units.message: n_spikes, first_spike_tick or last_spike_tick disagrees with core.spike_events
core.units.sql: SELECT u.session_id, u.unit_id FROM core_units u LEFT JOIN ( SELECT unit_id, COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(t_tick) AS lo, MAX(t_tick) AS hi FROM core_spike_events GROUP BY unit_id ) s USING (unit_id) WHERE (u.n_spikes IS NOT NULL AND u.n_spikes IS DISTINCT FROM COALESCE(s.n, 0)) OR (u.first_spike_tick IS NOT NULL AND u.first_spike_tick IS DISTINCT FROM s.lo) OR (u.last_spike_tick IS NOT NULL AND u.last_spike_tick IS DISTINCT FROM s.hi)

core.units.message: the designated quality label is not among the recorded ones
core.units.sql: SELECT u.session_id, u.unit_id, u.quality_label, u.quality_label_source FROM core_units u LEFT JOIN core_unit_quality_labels q ON u.unit_id = q.unit_id AND u.quality_label = q.normalized_label AND u.quality_label_source = q.source WHERE u.quality_label IS NOT NULL AND q.source IS NULL

core.units.message: quality_label and quality_label_source must be present together
core.units.sql: SELECT session_id, unit_id FROM core_units WHERE (quality_label IS NULL) <> (quality_label_source IS NULL)

core.units.message: units carry no observation intervals and their clock declares none, so no rate over them has a denominator
core.units.sql: SELECT u.session_id, u.unit_id FROM core_units u WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM core_unit_observation_intervals o WHERE o.unit_id = u.unit_id) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM core_clock_observation_intervals c WHERE c.session_id = u.session_id AND c.clock_id = u.clock_id)

core.units.message: a unit's spikes carry an amplitude and the unit declares no amplitude_unit (R96 §3.5)
core.units.sql: SELECT DISTINCT u.unit_id FROM core_spike_events s JOIN core_units u USING (unit_id) WHERE s.amplitude IS NOT NULL AND u.amplitude_unit IS NULL

core.clock_phase_steps.message: a phase step is recorded on a clock with no parent, and a step is a movement of the parent's phase (R99 3.3)
core.clock_phase_steps.sql: SELECT s.session_id, s.clock_id, s.t_tick FROM core_clock_phase_steps s JOIN core_clocks c ON c.session_id = s.session_id AND c.clock_id = s.clock_id WHERE c.parent_clock_id IS NULL

core.coordinate_frame_axes.message: two axes of one frame name the same field, so which axis a coordinate value sits on cannot be told (R105 3.2)
core.coordinate_frame_axes.sql: SELECT session_id, coordinate_frame, axis_name, COUNT(*) AS axes FROM core_coordinate_frame_axes GROUP BY session_id, coordinate_frame, axis_name HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

analysis.array_dimensions.message: an axis declares one half of its labelled coordinates; the resource says where the positions are and the column says which of its columns holds them (R100 2.2)
analysis.array_dimensions.sql: SELECT array_asset_id, axis_index, coordinate_resource, coordinate_position_column FROM analysis_array_dimensions WHERE (coordinate_resource IS NULL) <> (coordinate_position_column IS NULL)
